items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I was determined to hear Johnny Hodges... I said that I was studying music, and Johnny Hodges, my idol, was playing with the Duke Ellington band... And that's where I first heard Johnny Hodges and the Duke Ellington Orchestra. I didn't get a chance to say anything to any of them or anything

ctx.x: It was an alto saxophone, C.G. Conn, ha-ha, alto saxophone.

And I continued practicing... And I entered a contest at the Alamo Theatre, an amateur contest. That was the popular theatre, the Black theatre, the Alamo Theatre. And every Monday night they would have this talent contest. And my first entrance I won the first prize hands-down. You know, a kid playing alto saxophone... At that time, Johnny Hodges had made "Jeep's Blues," and it was popular; and I played "Jeep's Blues," you know...
